provenance.notes: The LAW was read instruction by instruction, by offline disassembly, out of the four routines the reference ships under their own names for this bake -- the orchestrator that runs the pass loop, the per-vertex blur stencil, the inward ring scan, and its buffer swap. No live run and no recording. (The symbol names and addresses are in the private capture record, toolcards/falloff.selection/bake_symbol_map.md, not here.) The WEIGHT TABLES below are computed from that law, which is why this is labelled analytic/closed-form rather than live-capture: they must not be counted as reference parity. They are anchored to the original 2026-07 capture by the four numbers in `anchors_recovered_from_the_original_capture`, every one of which this table reproduces exactly. The capture's own lookup-table files and its simulator did not survive (they lived in a scratch directory); these tables are the replacement, and the anchors are what make them trustworthy rather than merely self-consistent.

why_this_fixture_exists: Until 2026-08-20 this law existed only as prose in one agent's memory. Its raw evidence -- the 5x5 and 7x7 LUTs and the simulator that checked them -- was gone. A law with no frozen artefact is a law waiting to be re-measured, and this one cost a static read of four separate symbols to obtain.

rig.mesh: A 4-connected quad grid. The SELECTED region is an n x n block of vertices, embedded so that every vertex on the block's border has at least one UNSELECTED 4-neighbour. Nothing outside the block is ever evaluated.
rig.ring: ring(v) = 4-connected graph distance from the selection BORDER. Border vertices are ring 0. For an n x n block, ring(i,j) = min(i, j, n-1-i, n-1-j).
rig.layout: cases[].weights is row-major, weights[i][j] for i,j in 0..n-1.
rig.valence: Every non-border vertex of the block has exactly 4 in-block neighbours.

law.domain: The RAW selection only. The bake enumerates the selected flag and NEVER expands the moving set to unselected vertices.
law.boundary: Dirichlet-0. The blur stencil bails if ANY neighbour is unselected, so a selected vertex with an unselected neighbour is pinned at its seed and never blurred. With the seed rule below that pin is exactly 0.
law.seed: seed(v) = min(ring(v), S) / S, with S = max(steps, 1).
law.seed_sentinel_note: The cap is not cosmetic. The ring scan makes S+1 inward passes and vertices deeper than ring S keep a 1.0 sentinel from the no-qualifying-neighbour branch, which is what min(ring,S) expresses. Leaving them unset and letting the blur fill them is a DIFFERENT and measurably wrong law -- see rejected_candidates.
law.blur: Exactly 4 Jacobi passes, INDEPENDENT of steps (the loop compares against a literal 4). Each non-pinned vertex takes the uniform mean (1/valence) of its neighbours' weights. Self is NOT in the sum. A snapshot buffer makes it Jacobi, not Gauss-Seidel.
law.operator: The combinatorial GRAPH Laplacian -- uniform 1/valence weights. NOT cotangent, NOT edge-length weighted, NOT area weighted.
law.where_steps_acts: ENTIRELY in the ring seed ramp. The smoothing is a fixed 4 passes. That split is why every attempt to fit a single separable operator with a steps-dependent iteration count was underdetermined.
law.ease_applied_later: The evaluator applies smoothstep(w) = 3w^2 - 2w^3 to the RAW weight below. These tables are the RAW bake, before that ease.

rejected_candidates.verdict: REFUTED -- the loop compares against a literal 4; this is what OUR side does

falsifiers: steps=0 and steps=1 producing different tables (S = max(steps,1) makes them identical)
any weight at a border vertex other than exactly 0
any non-zero weight outside the selected block (the domain never expands)
a blur pass count that varies with steps
a neighbour mean that includes the vertex itself (would change every interior weight)
Gauss-Seidel sweeping instead of a snapshot buffer (order-dependent, and not dyadic)
any edge-length, cotangent or area term (all tabulated values are dyadic rationals; a geometric weight on a non-uniform grid could not be)
our_side_diverges: vibe3d's selection falloff is a DIFFERENT law and this fixture does not assert parity with it. Ours expands the moving set, makes the smoothing count steps-dependent (round(0.7*s^2+2)), and seeds hot rather than on the ring ramp. Three separate divergences, each one visible against the tables above. Closing them is a port task, not a fixture task.
